comments.author: Arda Guclu
comments.body:
This problem has existed from probably 4.15 (or even 4.14). Because to be FIPS compatible, we had to generate 2 different oc binaries per RHEL version and these versions don't work in another. Until 4.16, default oc is built on RHEL8.
That means, in 4.15 (maybe also in 4.14) the corresponding link  https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/4.16.0/openshift-client-linux-amd64-rhel9-4.16.0.tar.gz of them does not work on RHEL9, even though it says RHEL9 oc. After we switched the default oc to RHEL9, probably customers who are still on RHEL8 will try to get RHEL8 compatible binary and this link ^ is one of them. 
> Will the RHEL9 binary work on RHEL8? 
No, it doesn't work

comments.author: David Kaferad
comments.body:
Hello everyone!  Thanks for a further clarification. I'll start working on this task today (or during the weekend). I hope to have the necessary configuration changes to be done by Tuesday, but I can't give any promises for that. It's a time consuming task, and needs to be tested through every stage of the release process (before we can merge the changes). And every release job can take up to 4 hours. That's what makes it so time consuming on top of beign non-trivial... So I kindly ask you for your understanding and patience.
With that said, the plan is this:
- Update the product configuration so it fixes the issue for the future releases (as part of this ticket).

- Delete the previously released versions of oc binary on Customer Portal (for https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-8#icft=RHEL-8
).

- Re-run the release jobs (with the new configuration) per each deleted version from CP.

Given the time and resource complexity of the OCP release, we can only run them in serial to ensure we don't affect our overall release capacity in our pipeline for CLOUDDST products (ETERA). So the ultimate resolution time of the problem will depend on the number https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-8#icft=RHEL-8
 releases that were affected and need to be re-uploaded...
NOTE: The steps 2) and 3) will be tracked in a separate tickets.
Lastly, we will need your help with providing a list of affected OpenShift versions with the incorrect https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RHEL-8#icft=RHEL-8
 binaries. We no longer have Release Coordinators who could help us track that down... Thank you!

https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/4.16.3/ this is 4.16.3 artifacts are stored in.
Let's take architecture sample as amd64:

oc.rhel9 is https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/4.16.3/openshift-client-linux-amd64-rhel9-4.16.3.tar.gz or https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/4.16.3/openshift-client-linux-amd64-rhel9.tar.gz (they are identical)

comments.author: Kevin Myers
comments.body:
Case 03883437 was opened and attached to this issue.  
Customer downloaded the RHEL 8 (https://access.redhat.com/downloads/content/290/ver=4.16/rhel---8/4.16.2/x86_64/product-software) which does not work on RHEL 8.  As noted in this issue the download is identical to the RHEL 9  binary.  
This fails as it appears to have been built for RHEL 9 with a newer GLIBC version.  The binary works as expected on RHEL 9 and can confirm that both of these appear to be identical (matching sha256 checksum).
However this will not run on RHEL 8, giving these errors:
Example on RHEL 8:
$ ./oc --version
./oc: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.33' not found (required by ./oc)
./oc: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.34' not found (required by ./oc)
./oc: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.32' not found (required by ./oc)
Note:  The binary in the 'openshift-clients' RPM for from the repo 'rhocp-4.16-for-rhel-8-x86_64-rpms' does work on RHEL 8 as expected.

comments.author: David Kaferad
comments.body:
Hello @Hideshi Fukumoto,
my apologies for a late reply. I had to fully disconnect from JIRA notifications and Slack to work on this task - it required my full attention and deep work for several working days (including work in my off-hours).
The current status is that I had to rework from scratch the product config for OCP's clients / installers release process, and this work couldn't be started before we had all the necessary documentation for the OCP release process (which we didn't have until the creation of your ticket). To create a necessary documentation we basically did a Spike as part of this ticket...
Unfortunately, the necessary changes were not as easy as it might have sound from an outside view. With the need to differentiate between the RHEL8 and RHEL9, the complexity of the previous product config has basically squared. The original product config had over 1600 hundred lines of codes, and simply adding RHEL8 / RHEL9 was just not possible.
On top of that, each run of OCP release can take up to 4 hours, and it had to be run dozes of times during the config update to validate the progress. Every little typo resulted in a need to re-run the whole thing from scratch, which added a time complexity as well.
At this moment, I have MR in place, and I'm waiting for an approval from my colleagues - we should have it merged by the end of today. After that all the future releases of OCP (4.15+) should now be done as intended.
To address the previous incorrect releases, I'll need you to create a new ticket for us, where we will track the follow-up work needed there.
For now, the previous macOS / Windows releases should work as expected, and the previous Linux clients / installers can be obtained from here (as workaround):
- https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/ (MOC)

Therefore I have lowered the criticality of this ticket, because there's an existing workaround. Please note that the Linux clients / installer (either for RHEL8 or RHEL9) from MOC are identical to what we provide to our customers via downloads in Customer Portal, so this workaround is safe to use.
Last, but not least - I would ask you to not you a passive-aggressive tone in your messages next time - it really didn't help anything. Thank you!
With best regards,
Dee'Kej

Please fill out all the relevant fields below as best as you can. This will help us better understand your issue and its severity. Thank you!
- Product: OpenShift

- Component: oc

- Version: 4.14 through 4.16 (and possibly 4.17)

- Architecture: linux/*

Problem description: 
As oc maintainers, we have started generating 2 different oc binaries built on RHEL9 and RHEL8 and the default oc is built on RHEL9. 
Since https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/etera-service/product-configs/-/blob/latest/RHOSE.yml?ref_type=heads#L28 relies on the default oc (https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/4.16.0/openshift-client-linux-4.16.0.tar.gz ), 
https://access.redhat.com/downloads/content/290/ver=4.16/rhel---8/4.16.0/x86_64/product-software page refers to oc that is built on RHEL9 incorrectly. 
I'd recommend instead of relying on the default oc, it is better to stick to the RHEL version.

Up until now we were releasing OCP the way we always did - without questioning why we do it this way and asking if it can be improved in some ways...

Just a quick update, summarizing the ART work I know about.  Most of it can be summarized as Konflux release automation:
In the last week we’ve made it so we can attach CVEs to shipments*, we can build shipments metadata from assemblies, we improved shipments CI, we made it impossible to ship in the presence of blocker bugs and we created the missing Release Plans and Release Plan Admission for OCP releases.  We even stopped building 4.20 in OSBS.
- A "shipment" is an internal ART object that allows them to keep track of everything going into a Konflux errata.

comments.author: Brenton Leanhardt
comments.body:
ART Summary:
Since Container Health Index scores are lost with our move to Konflux we're working to come up with a replacement.  The CHI is an important way ART makes sure we don't accidentally ship vulnerable code.
Our biggest risks:
- OpenShift releases one container image to many repositories.  This jira is a blocker for OCP.

- It seems like multi-component builds are not working correctly with File-Based Catalogs.

- We're still struggling with performance.  In some cases it's things like Merge Requests taking a long time but there are more serious issues.  Andrew McNamara is aware and has made enormous progress, but the fixes aren't in production yet.

comments.author: Ernesto Gonzalez Chacon
comments.body:
Hello team,
We've added a Repository Migration Status table to your tracker to help track the progress of your repositories' migration to Konflux.
How to use this table:
1. Konflux Migration Status - This column is automatically updated by our system and shows the current migration status of each repository based on our data.
2. Dev Team Status - Please update this column with your team's perspective on the migration status. Use values like:
- "Building" - Image is configured and building in Konflux

- "Testing" - Image is built and being tested in Konflux.

- "Waiting to Release" - Image is ready but waiting for release approval. RPA's are there but not yet released.

- "Released" - Image is fully released with Konflux

3. Comments/Observations - Use this column to add any relevant notes, blockers, or observations about the migration process.
Please review and update the table regularly to help us track your team's migration progress accurately.
Note: If you have deprecated images please let us know in the "Comments/Observations" column, and:
- If they are in Pyxis, mark them as deprecated in the Comet UI so they don't show up in our metrics anymore.

- If they are in App-Interface, stop deploying them.

If you have any questions about this table or need assistance with your migration, please don't hesitate to reach out.
Thank you for your cooperation!
Konflux Migration Team

comments.author: Brenton Leanhardt
comments.body:
It's been a tough week for us.  We’ve hit three new blockers in the last three days.  With the Konflux team's help two of them were resolved quickly.
The unsolved problem is well understood, even if the exact fix is still unknown.  It's actually the result of recent Conforma scaling improvements we needed---scaling Conforma is hitting Quay rate limits.  We’re working with the Konflux team and the Quay team to figure out a solution.
The challenge is that this is happening at really unfortunate time. Next Monday marks the deadline for when we said we needed zero blockers in order to gather the evidence that our platform is able to mean OCP release demands.  Hitting three new blockers this week has us worried.
In other news:
- Justin solved two QE challenges we’ve been facing.  
- The first involves a design for optional operator teams QE teams where ART will be informed early if there have been changes that impact Conforma.  

- The second was a solution to a File-Based Catalog problem our Errata Reliability team was hitting.


- ART landed several tooling fixes required for mitgration (https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ART-13330,  https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ART-12596 , https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/ART-13868)

Support for multiple product_id is needed to support future RHEL rpm releases, similarly like it's supported today in the Errata Tool. 2) And currently the advisory is container advisory, should we support rpm type and module type?
Will it be included in these features (KONFLUX-6854, KONFLUX-3868)?
I mean we only need to support in container konflux, not need support rpm and module now

I have been told our goal is to ship a large percentage of rpms in konflux by the end of CY25. I do not have any more specific details of when we will start work on that stuff though. Andrew McNamara do you have any details about when rpm stuff will start in konflux?
 
 
The main purpose of the multiple CPE support is to cover RPM / module RPMs content release.
For container type content we push users now to use separate advisories for containers built based on RHEL8 and RHEL9.
3) If yes, how to distinguish an advisory that belongs to which type of advisory?
     Is there a tag in the schema, or use a different schema for each type?

Content type is represented by the component purl and purl type (oci, rpm, rpmmod).
Based on the official purl guidelines: https://redhatproductsecurity.github.io/security-data-guidelines/purl/
 
I would propose to suspend any work on the multiple CPE support until we don't have Konflux RPA and Advisory spec for that.

SECDATA-878.description:
Title / Epic Summary
Support for multiple CPEs in Konflux Advisory OR support for multiple CPEs and RPM-based content in Konflux Advisory, based on CY25Q2 and CY25Q3 external factors (Konflux team will say which it is when the time comes).
Outcome
Desired outcome: SDEngine processes Konflux Advisories based on a new (not yet existing as of CY25Q1) schema that includes multiple CPEs or multiple CPEs and RPMs. This is then used similarly to errata tool advisories to generate content for CVE pages, CSAF, VEX, OVAL.
Acceptance Criteria
- SDEngine consumes konflux advisories from https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/releng/advisories/-/blob/main/data/advisories .

- The advisories are in a format described by a specification, such as https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/releng/advisories/-/blob/main/schema/advisory.json?ref_type=heads

- The specification is different from the specification already used in production as of CY25Q1 and includes the new features (multiple CPEs, RPMs).

- Konflux and SDEngine teams agree on that specificaiton and agree on a specific date and time when both teams/systems switch from the old format to the new format.

- The change happens successfully, SDEngine processes the advisories (see point 1) correctly.

Details
Are there any specifications or details relevant to this request?
TBD, but also see below
Relevant Stakeholders
On Konflux side:
@Johnny Bieren 
@Przemyslaw Roguski 
On SDEngine side:
@Chuntao Han (Hank)
@Jakub Svoboda 
Impact Statement
What is the impact of this request? For example: How many users are impacted? How much money is saved? What are the consequences if we don't do this?
Understanding of the Impact Statement requires understanding of the reason Konflux and SDEngine projects exist. Such understanding then means the impact is clear.
So to state the obvious: This is critical and enables Red Hat's continued stream of information to CVE Pages, CSAF, VEX, OVAL. It impacts all Red Hat and most customers, many non-customers, RH's reputation. Probably saves untold amount of money in fines. I'm not able to properly list the consequences of not doing this.
Target Start Date
What is the desired start of the Epic? Are there any due dates or delivery expectations? If so please explain.
Start probably CY25Q2 or CY25Q3 based on input from Konflux team.
SDEngine can't do anything without Konflux team first creating a new version of the advisory spec (at least draft). That might change based on external factors that put a pressure on Konflux directly (not on SDEngine directly).
Possible preparation on SDEngine side already done (see comments, there are links to documents and drawings; two SDEngine engineers are already reasonably familiar with the code structure to be able to start the implementation when the time comes).
(the above written on 2025-03-12 based on the meeting "Resolve questions on multiple cpe id support" with Rogue, Yuli, Hank, Jakub, Marek)

Original Description as written by John Bieren:
(Leaving the original description without edits, because it captures the viewpoint of the Konflux team, which is different enough that I would miss important nuances.)
 
Title / Epic Summary
Support multiple cpe id in konflux advisory.
Outcome
In some cases users want to release one update to many product versions or supported channels, which is represented by many EngIDs and sometimes many CPE ids. This is a typical use case in RHEL products. In the container based products many times users want to mix RHEL8 based images with RHEL9 based images, which requires associations with more than one CPE id.
Hence we need to specify a CPE id as a list in the Konflux advisories.
For CPE id we need precise mapping between CPE (product variant) and component.
 
Acceptance Criteria
SDEngine can consume new Konflux advisory schema and produce correct content in the security metadata (CVE pages and CSAF/VEX files).
This include mapping between CPE id to product and component.
 
Relevant Stakeholders
On Konflux side:
@Johnny Bieren 
@Przemyslaw Roguski 
Impact Statement
Once Konflux is used to release RPM content, then this functionality will be critical. Which is Q2/2025 as I understand.
For the container container this is nice to have functionality, but is not critical.
 
Target Start Date
It would be good to have this functionality ready to use in at the beginning of Q2/2025 (there is no hard target GA date)
